incident.title: Revenue down 45% and finance suspects the pipeline
incident.alert: The executive revenue dashboard shows daily revenue down roughly 45% since 2026-07-01 and it has not recovered. Finance suspects a pipeline fault.

request.query: SELECT order_date, revenue_usd FROM mart_daily_revenue WHERE order_date >= '2026-06-27' ORDER BY order_date LIMIT 6

trace.plain: Looked at the revenue report — it halves on July 1st.

request.query: SELECT order_date, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(SUM(amount)/100.0,2) src FROM raw_orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-06-27' GROUP BY order_date ORDER BY order_date LIMIT 6

observation.note: the decline is present in the source extract itself

trace.plain: Checked the raw source data — the same drop is already there.
Read the delivery logs — every batch arrived complete.

observation.note: no transform changed in or before the anomaly window

trace.plain: Checked the change history — nobody changed the pipeline.
Checked the data format — unchanged since May.
Checked how fresh the data is — one day old, as expected.
Ran the built-in consistency checks — all passed.

lines: 2026-06-29  Two regional distributors ended their contracts effective 2026-07-01.

trace.plain: Read the business notices — two distributors ended their contracts on July 1st.

decision.claim: The pipeline is sound and the movement is real. Daily order counts fall by the same proportion in the raw source extract, every delivery window reconciles, no transform changed, and the drop is independently explained by two distributor contracts ending on the same date.

evaluation.note: Proposing no change was the correct action. Restraint is a result, not an absence of one.

intro.question: Did the pipeline break, or did the business change?
intro.decision: The drop is already in the source data. Two distributors left.
intro.takeaway: The data is correct. Fixing it would have created an error.
